title: Customer registration, sign-in and account protection
context: As a customer I want to register and sign in, and I want my account protected against password guessing. Covers registration (POST /users/register), sign-in via API and web shop, lockout after repeated wrong passwords, and sign-out token invalidation.

sourcesRead.contributes: User story (L17), identity API endpoints, login response shape, Bearer auth and web shop sign-in entry (L19), and the seven Gherkin acceptance criteria (L23-L60). No attachments, no comments.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: Registration creates the customer without echoing the password. Given a new customer with a unique e-mail address, When their details are posted to POST /users/register, Then the API responds 201 with the customer's details and an id, And the response does not contain the password
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Registration creates the customer without echoing the password Given a new customer with a unique e-mail address When their details are posted to POST /users/register Then the API responds 201 with the customer's details and an id And the response does not contain the password
outcomes: the response contains the customer's details and an id
the response does not contain the password

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: A registered e-mail address cannot register twice. Given a customer already registered with an e-mail address, When the same e-mail address is registered again, Then the API responds 409 with the message "A customer with this email address already exists."
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: A registered e-mail address cannot register twice Given a customer already registered with an e-mail address When the same e-mail address is registered again Then the API responds 409 with the message "A customer with this email address already exists."
outcomes: second registration with the same e-mail address responds 409
message "A customer with this email address already exists."

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: Weak passwords are rejected with every broken rule listed. Given a new customer whose password is "abc", When they register, Then the API responds 422 and the password errors state all four rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Weak passwords are rejected with every broken rule listed Given a new customer whose password is "abc" When they register Then the API responds 422 and the password errors state all four rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number
outcomes: the password errors state the rule: at least 8 characters
the password errors state the rule: upper and lower case letters
the password errors state the rule: a symbol
the password errors state the rule: a number

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: Signing in on the web shop. Given a registered customer on the web shop's sign-in page, When they sign in with their e-mail address and password, Then they land on the "My account" page, And the navigation shows their first and last name
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Signing in on the web shop Given a registered customer on the web shop's sign-in page When they sign in with their e-mail address and password Then they land on the "My account" page And the navigation shows their first and last name
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop sign-in page ("Sign in" in the navigation, see G3)
outcomes: after signing in they land on the "My account" page
the navigation shows the customer's first and last name

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: A wrong password is refused. Given a registered customer, When they sign in with a wrong password, Then POST /users/login responds 401, And the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: A wrong password is refused Given a registered customer When they sign in with a wrong password Then POST /users/login responds 401 And the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop sign-in page ("Sign in" in the navigation, see G3)
outcomes: POST /users/login with a wrong password responds 401
the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: The account locks after five failed attempts. Given a registered customer, When five sign-in attempts with a wrong password are made, Then attempts one to five respond 401, And the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423 with a message that the account is locked
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: The account locks after five failed attempts Given a registered customer When five sign-in attempts with a wrong password are made Then attempts one to five respond 401 And the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423 with a message that the account is locked
outcomes: wrong-password sign-in attempts one to five each respond 401
the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423
the sixth attempt's response has a message that the account is locked

acceptanceCriteria.text: Scenario: Signing out invalidates the token. Given a signed-in customer with an access token, When they sign out with GET /users/logout, Then GET /users/me with the same token responds 401
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Scenario: Signing out invalidates the token Given a signed-in customer with an access token When they sign out with GET /users/logout Then GET /users/me with the same token responds 401
outcomes: after GET /users/logout, GET /users/me with the same token responds 401

endpoints.request: JSON: first_name, last_name, dob, address {street, city, state, country, postal_code}, phone, email, password (field names: G1)
endpoints.success: 201 with the customer's details and an id, without the password (AC-1)

rules.text: Password rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number; a registration breaking them is rejected with 422 and every broken rule listed
An e-mail address can be registered only once; a second registration responds 409
The account locks after five failed sign-in attempts: attempts one to five respond 401, the sixth attempt responds 423 even with the correct password
The registration response never contains the password
Signing out invalidates the access token: GET /users/me with that token then responds 401

errorModel.case: registering an e-mail address that is already registered (POST /users/register)
errorModel.body: A customer with this email address already exists.

errorModel.case: registering with a weak password (POST /users/register): password errors state every broken rule
signing in with a wrong password (POST /users/login), including failed attempts one to five
signing in with a wrong password on the web shop: message shown on the sign-in page (UI text, not an API body)
sign-in after five failed attempts, even with the correct password (POST /users/login): message that the account is locked (wording not specified, G6)
GET /users/me with a token that was signed out via GET /users/logout

auth.mechanism: Authorization: Bearer <access_token> on GET /users/me and GET /users/logout; the access_token comes from POST /users/login

testData.strategy: Each test registers its own customer via POST /users/register with a unique e-mail address at example.com and the payload fields of G1; signed-in state comes from POST /users/login with that customer's e-mail address and password.
constraints: E-mail addresses must be unique per run (AC-1 requires a new customer; AC-2 relies on a first registration succeeding)
The lockout scenario (AC-6) locks its customer: use a dedicated customer and never reuse it
Customers cannot delete themselves (deleting a user needs the admin role), so created customers stay in the shared sandbox
testData.cleanup: none possible without admin rights; unique e-mail addresses keep runs independent
